reasoning:
NVIDIA is a simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generative business with one of the widest moats in technology, and I mean that precisely. The moat is the CUDA software ecosystem layered on top of the best accelerated silicon, reinforced by full-system integration and networking. Switching costs for the developer base and the hyperscaler install base are enormous. That's the quality bar I require.

The financials are pristine. Free cash flow was $96.7B last fiscal year, up from $61B the year prior, and the balance sheet carries net cash of $51B against trivial debt, so net debt to EBITDA is meaningfully negative. Operating margins above 60% with gross margins in the low-70s. This is the kind of capital-light, high-return compounder I'd happily concentrate in. Management runs it with discipline: $40B of buybacks last year funded entirely from internal cash, no leverage engineering.

Where I have to be honest is valuation and the absence of an activist angle. On trailing free cash flow the yield is under 1%, which is rich, and EV to FCF is well over 50x trailing. The bull case rests on forward FCF, which the Street has roughly doubling over two years; if that ramp holds, EV/FCF normalizes toward 30x and the stock is reasonable, even cheap for the quality. There's no activism to do here, the company is already exceptionally well run, so I'm underwriting pure quality plus a growth runway rather than a value-unlock. My intrinsic value, on a forward-FCF DCF with a demanding cost of capital, lands roughly in line with the current price, modest margin of safety at best. I'd own it as a quality compounder and add on volatility. Bullish, but sized for the fact that the multiple already pays for several years of execution.

key_metrics.activist_catalyst: None; company is already optimally run. Thesis is quality + growth, not value-unlock.

data_gaps: EV/FCF on forward FCF requires Street estimates; trailing EV/FCF shown
